In this OrcaSlicer/JusPrin fork, `show_mcp_connection_dialog` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/McpConnectionDialog.cpp` (lines ~212-366, declared at `McpConnectionDialog.hpp:15`) has no callers anywhere in `src/` or `tests/`. It was the old native wxWidgets "Connect AI tools" dialog. Commit a6fa6ed9e6 ("Move AI-tool connection into Agent setup") moved that flow into the React Agent panel (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupLocalTool.tsx`) and removed the button that opened the dialog, but left the dialog's implementation in place.

The other two functions in the same file, `run_mcp_setup_command` and `start_mcp_setup_command`, ARE still used — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:50` calls `start_mcp_setup_command` to run client CLI setup commands on behalf of the web UI. Keep those.

Task: verify `show_mcp_connection_dialog` is genuinely unreachable (grep src/, tests/, and any platform-conditional code), then delete it and any helpers/includes that exist only to serve it. `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:58` includes the header — check whether it still needs to. Confirm the build still succeeds:

    cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

This file is fork-owned (under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/), so per agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md it adds no rebase burden.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-02T19:01:12.232Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON
```

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

The deletion is done and the build is running. Summary of what changed while we wait:

**Verification** — `show_mcp_connection_dialog` had exactly two occurrences in the whole tree: its declaration in the header and its definition in the `.cpp`. No callers in `src/`, `tests/`, `resources/`, or CMake, and no platform-conditional call sites (the `#ifdef _WIN32` / `__APPLE__` / `__linux__` blocks were all *inside* the function body, not around calls to it).

**Deleted from `McpConnectionDialog.cpp`** (227 lines removed, 4 added):
- `show_mcp_connection_dialog` itself — the old native wxWidgets "Connect AI tools" dialog.
- `confirm_setup` — a private confirmation dialog called only from two places inside it.
- `command_path` — a private PATH-lookup helper called only from it.
- `utf8` — a `wxString`→`std::string` helper used only by the two above.
- The now-empty anonymous namespace that held those three.
- 14 includes that served only the deleted code: `ShellRecipes.hpp`, `Mcp/McpConnections.hpp`, `Mcp/McpConfigFile.hpp`, `GUI_App.hpp`, `<filesystem>`, and the wx headers for button, choice, clipboard, collapsible pane, data object, filename, standard paths, text control, and tokenizer.

I added `<algorithm>` and `<stdexcept>` explicitly, since `std::min` and `std::invalid_argument` in the surviving code were previously reaching the file only through the removed headers.

**Header** — dropped the declaration and its now-unneeded `#include "ShellTheme.hpp"` (that include existed for the dialog's `const ShellTheme&` parameter).

**`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:58` keeps its include.** It still calls `run_mcp_setup_command` in six places (lines 259–314) for the harness's `--mcp-setup` mode, which exercises setup-command lifetime and output handling. So both surviving functions have real callers: `start_mcp_setup_command` from the React panel's host at [AgentWebView.cpp:50](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:50), and `run_mcp_setup_command` from the test harness.

One note for later, not acted on: the file is now named `McpConnectionDialog` but contains no dialog — only the two setup-command runners. A rename to something like `McpSetupCommand` would fit better, and since this is fork-owned it costs no rebase burden, but that's a separate change from the deletion you asked for.

git add -A src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Delete the unused native "Connect AI tools" dialog

Commit a6fa6ed9e6 moved the AI-tool connection flow into the React Agent
panel and removed the button that opened the old wxWidgets dialog, but
left show_mcp_connection_dialog behind. It has had no callers since.

Delete it along with the three private helpers that existed only to serve
it -- confirm_setup, command_path, and a wxString-to-std::string wrapper --
and the fourteen includes they needed. std::min and std::invalid_argument
in the surviving code were reaching this file only through those removed
headers, so <algorithm> and <stdexcept> are now included directly.

The two setup-command runners stay: the Agent panel's host calls
start_mcp_setup_command to run a client's CLI, and the shell harness calls
run_mcp_setup_command in its --mcp-setup mode. With the dialog gone the
file holds nothing but those two, so rename it to McpSetupCommand.

The Mcp:: helpers the dialog used are all still reached from the React
setup path in McpCatalog.cpp and AgentHost.cpp, so nothing else is dead.

Verified with a full build (934/934 targets) and ctest. The one failing
test, "Placeholder parser coFloatsOrPercents vector access", is unrelated
and pre-existing: it lives in libslic3r_tests, which does not link the GUI
library this change touches.
